title: Boundaries of Control
hook: Half the stuff keeping you up at night isn't even yours to fix.
statement: Put your energy into what you can actually control. Everything else is just expensive worrying.
explainer: The same effort spent on something you can't move produces nothing. Spent on something you can, it compounds. It's not about caring less. It's about caring in the right spot.
sop: Write down everything on your mind right now.
Sort each item into Control, Influence, or No Control.
Score Control and Effort from 1 to 10 for each one.
Pull your effort off the No Control pile completely.
Recheck weekly, since some items quietly move into Influence.
equation_example: Control 8, Effort 7. 8 × 7 = 56 Efficiency. Now Control 2, same Effort 7. 2 × 7 = 14. Same hustle, a quarter of the payoff. Higher means your effort is landing. Lower means you're working hard against a wall.
question: Write down one worry you can't control, then name the one piece of it you can.
closing_statement: Effort only compounds where you actually have control.
caption:
Principle Nº 230: Boundaries of Control

Half the stuff keeping you up at night isn't even yours to fix.

Put your energy into what you can actually control. Everything else is just expensive worrying.
